criteria.rationale: Verified optional-policy fallback, explicit runner selection and the R1-F1 correction. D1 assigns root bindings to the instance runner; their correctness remains an instance responsibility. Path validation assumes a trusted local checkout remains stable until execution and provides no hostile-filesystem containment guarantee.
The new path synchronously waits for one child and introduces no shared mutable state or background lifecycle. Examined process IO, wait and exit handling.
The optional schema-1 policy adds delegation while preserving existing hook behavior when absent.
Examined strict decoding, EOF enforcement, schema, local-path, confinement, regular-file and executable checks, plus launch failures.
Traced main.go invocation-name dispatch through HookMain to the declared runner and reviewed launch-inventory registration.
Policy and launch errors identify their context; status identifies delegation or refusal, and runner output is forwarded.
Examined absent-policy branches and existing installation behavior. Original pre-commit and post-merge subcommands remain unchanged; no MCP contract changes.
Focused tests passed independently. Inspected project-root cwd, hook-name argument, exit propagation and refusal paths.

D1 addresses hooks losing instance-provided root bindings by invoking the instance runner. HookMain delegates before its legacy dispatch, while the engine gains no mechanism for granting root authority. No structural facts requiring individual mappings were supplied.
Reviewed English and Portuguese manuals and both scaffold copies against the runtime policy, argument, exit-code, status and refusal behavior. Scaffold and locale tests passed independently.
Status exposes the selected runner or refusal reason; hook failures identify policy or execution errors and preserve runner diagnostics.

Mapped R1 to runner execution and exit tests, R2 to validation and negative tests, and R3 to managed-hook status. Reviewed cwd and symlink-confinement implementation and ran the confinement regression.

Implementation, tests, launch inventory, validation registration and documentation match the declared artifacts and R1-R3. Artifact reconciliation found no errors; root-resolution authority is unchanged.

Examined direct argv execution, strict policy refusal, absolute and escaping paths, symlink confinement, regular-file and executable checks. No shell interpolation or new root-authority mechanism was introduced.

One optional policy reader and synchronous runner invocation are sufficient for R1-R3. D1 avoids expanding engine root-authority configuration. No runner framework or speculative extension mechanism was added; a future requirement for untrusted execution would require a different design.
